title: Pauri 7, sound: je jug chaare
hookLine: je jug chaare aarjaa hor dasoonee hoe

cards: If you could live as long as you wanted, how long would you choose? A hundred years? A thousand?
People have always dreamed about it, from old legends of sages who lived for ages to today's headlines about slowing down aging.

The seventh pauri of Japji opens with that dream and makes it enormous: a life as long as all four ages of the world, and then ten times more. It's a line about time, and it sounds like it's stretching.

teach.h: JUG — AN AGE. CHAARE — ALL FOUR.
teach.b: The opening line: je jug chaare aarjaa, hor dasoonee hoe. Je: jay, if. Jug: like the English word jug, but shorter, closer to joog; it's an age, an era.
You met it inside jugaad, through the ages. Chaare: CHAA-ray, all four; in Indian thought, time turns through four great ages, the four jugs.
Aarjaa: AAR-jaa, a lifespan. Hor: and more. Dasoonee: da-SOO-nee, tenfold.
Hoe: HO-ay, it were. If your lifespan were all four ages, and ten times more. The meaning, and a surprising twist, come tomorrow.
Today, the sound. The line opens with short, quick words, je, jug, then gets longer: chaare, aarjaa, dasoonee. The syllables stretch, like the lifetime they describe.

The next lines keep adding: nav khandaa vich jaaneeai, known in all nine regions of the world. Naal chalai sabh koe, with everyone walking along beside you. Changaa naau rakhaae kai, keeping a good name.
Jas keerat jag lei, praise and fame in the world.
Long life, fame, followers, reputation: a list getting bigger and bigger.
And just when it's at its tallest, the pauri turns on a single short word: je.

how: The seventh pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its long opening line about living through the four ages is one of the most memorable in the hymn.

o: an age, a great era of the world
the lifetime of a single person
a clay pot for carrying water

games.q: match the sound to its sense.

s: the line imagines a life as long as all four ages, and ten times more
je jug chaare aarjaa, hor dasoonee hoe.
jug here means a water jug
it's an age of the world; you met it inside jugaad.
pauri seven's list gets shorter as it goes
it piles up: long life, fame, followers, a good name.

games.q: the pauri's list is at its tallest: long life, fame, followers, a good name. what short word turns it?
games.why: je, if. the turn comes tomorrow.

practice: Say it slowly, out loud if you can, and let the long words stretch: je jug chaare aarjaa, hor dasoonee hoe. Say it twice more, the last time softly.
Then sit and feel how long this one breath is, the only length of life you actually have in your hands right now; if you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Jug. An age, an era: four of them stacked and multiplied tenfold, je jug chaare, in this pauri's opening dream of a life.

carryVoice: Your line: je jug chaare. Looking back: saachaa saahib, nadar and the early hour, thaapiaa na jaae, one Giver, teerath naavaa, and jewels within. A whole week of Japji, and day one hundred seventy-five.
